diagram_candidates.claim: Each directed vertex v is replaced by the path v_1-v_2-v_3; each directed arc (u,v) becomes the undirected cross-edge u_3-v_1. Degree two at v_2 forces traversal through the three-vertex gadget, and the 3-to-1 orientation of cross-edges forces all gadgets to be traversed consistently.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The direction encoding and converse orientation argument are the central map and are easier to inspect in a small labelled gadget plus a cyclic chain schematic.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Show a single vertex gadget v_1—v_2—v_3, with v_2 degree two; show an arc u→v becoming only the undirected cross-edge u_3—v_1; then show the cycle order v^(1)_1,v^(1)_2,v^(1)_3,…,v^(n)_1,v^(n)_2,v^(n)_3,v^(1)_1. Label the arrows as the source orientation and the line edges as the target graph. Do not imply cross-edges in both endpoint orientations.
